name: LLM Adapter — Amazon Bedrock
description: Adds Amazon Bedrock as an LLM provider (Converse API) to the llm-adapter router via the provider-registration seam — no base files overwritten. Auth uses the AWS credential chain; install @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime.

questions.prompt: Default AWS region for Bedrock? (code never hardcodes it — the SDK cascade resolves region; this only seeds .env.bedrock.example)
Default Bedrock inference-profile model id? (override per tier via BEDROCK_*_MODEL)
Wire optional Bedrock Guardrails support (attached when BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID is set)?

checklist: Install the AWS SDK — the only channel, since manifests have no deps field: npm install @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime
Enable model access for your chosen Bedrock model in the Bedrock console (per account, per region) — calls return AccessDeniedException until you do
Import the registration once at startup, before constructing the router: import './infrastructure/llm/adapters/bedrock-register'
Make Bedrock the router's primary provider: new LLMRouter('bedrock')
Auth uses the AWS credential chain — on ECS/Graviton leave AWS_* unset and grant the task role bedrock:InvokeModel / bedrock:Converse; set AWS_* in .env.local for local dev
Override model ids per tier via BEDROCK_REASONING_MODEL / BEDROCK_FAST_MODEL / BEDROCK_VISION_MODEL if the install default doesn't fit
If using Guardrails, set BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID (and optionally BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION)
